text:
Priya Shah: Looping in the team on an urgent customer escalation from AcmeAppOps — they're getting 429s even though they think they're under quota. Customer says bursty traffic from a CDN changed IPs last night and they rotated keys this morning. copied logs below.

Devin (AcmeAppOps): we started seeing spikes ~02:10 UTC, then steady 429s. no code changes. traffic is mostly from one egress IP (our CDN). this is blocking production.

Devin (AcmeAppOps): sample curl from worker pool:
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-xxxx" \
  -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":20}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

Devin (AcmeAppOps): response headers:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 12
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1200
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Scope: org:acct-9876
```

Devin (AcmeAppOps): our dashboard (project level) shows 40% usage of the project quota. why is X-RateLimit-Scope org:acct-9876? we use project keys.

Priya Shah: thanks — can you paste the exact Authorization header (safely masked) and the key id from dashboard? also confirm if you switched from a project key to an org key when you rotated.

Devin (AcmeAppOps): masked key: sk-p_abc... we definitely rotated via the console under the project: projects/acme-web -> API keys -> rotate. UI showed new key created with label 'daemon'. we have a previous key still active while we roll.

Carlos (SRE): quick note — X-RateLimit-Scope header showing org means the enforcement happened against an org-level aggregate bucket, not project. possible causes: org-wide burst rule, or a super-key (org token) was used. can you confirm the key id (starts with sk-org- vs sk-p_)?

Devin (AcmeAppOps): key id (from console) is sk-p_abc123. but the token we posted in the curl was from our env secret store — maybe someone swapped a different secret into the pool. i'm checking.

Devin (AcmeAppOps): also: our CDN egress changed to 3 IPs last night (NAT). could IP-based limits be kicking in?

Marta (Eng): short expl: our limits stack in this order when applicable: per-key -> per-project -> per-org -> IP-based burst caps. When a request matches multiple scopes, the strictest applicable limiter may return the 429 and the header shows the scope that triggered enforcement. The X-RateLimit-Scope value indicates which quota was hit.

Marta (Eng): edge cases:
- if a key is a "project key" but the request includes an org-level authorization header (rare), enforcement picks org scope.
- temporary tokens minted by the control plane can be charged to the org bucket depending on how they were created.

rate-limit-bot: Policy snippet: "Org-level burst windows: 2m burst @ 2k rps, sustained org quota applied at 1m window. IP-based sync limiter: 500 rps per single IPv4 NAT ip. Project quotas are independent but summed all projects contribute to org accounting."

Devin (AcmeAppOps): okay we found two things: (1) our secret rotation script accidentally wrote the org-level token (sk-org-..) into the pool for a short window, (2) our CDN concentrated traffic to one IP so IP-based burst also hit. both may have overlapped.

Priya Shah: that explains the header showing org. good find. Devin, can you share timestamps for when the org token was used and when the IP concentration happened? we can correlate with logs.

Devin (AcmeAppOps): org token used between 02:09:32 and 02:12:05 UTC. CDN egress IP 52.44.210.11 had a spike 02:08–02:15.

Carlos (SRE): pulled internal logs for acct-9876: we see a spike at 02:09:40 from 52.44.210.11 hitting ~2100 rps -> org-level burst guard tripped at 02:09:45, returning 429s with X-RateLimit-Scope: org:acct-9876. also saw several connections with Authorization header starting sk-org-.

Carlos (SRE): after 02:12:10 the org token usage stops and rates drop. aggregate project usage remained ~30% so project quota wasn't the problem.

Devin (AcmeAppOps): so which limiter caused the 429s we saw? org burst or IP limiter? both?

Marta (Eng): both contributed. sequence: org token caused requests to be counted against org bucket; because the org bucket was already near burst limit due to other projects, the added load pushed it over the threshold. Simultaneously, the NATed IP crossed the IP-based burst threshold which causes short-term rejects for that IP. Our system will surface the first enforcement that returns a 429; header shows the scope. If both apply you may see org scope 429s first.

Jin (Billing): quick billing note — if a project-level spend cap is hit we return 402/403 depending on stage, not 429. no billing action here. customer account shows no spend cap triggered.

Devin (AcmeAppOps): thanks. what's the recommended mitigation to avoid this in future?

Marta (Eng): actionable suggestions:
- don't store org keys in worker pools; use project keys or short-lived tokens created under the project.
- add jittered client retries respecting Retry-After header.
- request an IP exemption for your CDN egress if you have predictable, high-volume NATed IPs (we can whitelist for higher burst).
- if you need sustained higher ingest, request a project quota increase or a dedicated capacity reservation (Dedicated) to avoid org-level contention.

Priya Shah: I've proposed a temporary remission: we'll scrub the 429s from the customer's incident metrics window since this was caused by mis-configured key rotation. Devin, can you confirm you rotated the pool to the correct sk-p_ key and rotated secrets in all replicas?

Devin (AcmeAppOps): yes — rotation complete and new key is in all pods (confirmed at 02:20 UTC). we've also requested a static egress IP from CDN vendor.

Carlos (SRE): follow-up: we'll add a server-side alert for org-level token usage that suddenly spikes from a project. that should catch accidental org-key leakage earlier.

Marta (Eng): also pushing a docs tweak: clarify that "project-rotations" create new project keys by default but copying/pasting in the console can accidentally pick org tokens. small UI wording fix.

Priya Shah: closing loop with customer: Devin, I'll email you a postmortem and the scrub/remediation details. ping here if you see anything else. :thumbsup:

Devin (AcmeAppOps): thanks everyone — huge help. saved our morning. :raised_hands:
